results.title: Together AI Pricing (October 2026): Serverless, Dedicated & GPU Clusters | Morph
results.author: Morph Team
highlights:
October 11, 2026 · 12 min read

## Together AI Serverless Per-Token Pricing (October 2026)

Serverless is the pay-per-token tier: no capacity to reserve, you are billed on input and output tokens and share a rate-limited pool with other users. All prices below are per million tokens (MTok), from the Together pricing page as of October 11, 2026. Cached input, where offered, is billed at a steep discount when the same prompt prefix repeats.

...

A dedicated endpoint is single-tenant serving: Together provisions the GPUs, runs the model, and bills you by the hour whether or not traffic is flowing. This is the tier for steady, high-volume production where serverless rate limits get in the way. Published hourly rates as of July 2026:

$5.49/hr NVIDIA HGX H100 (dedicated)

$8.99/hr NVIDIA HGX B200 (dedicated)

...

## GPU Clusters: Renting Raw Compute

One tier below managed dedicated endpoints, Together rents raw GPU clusters where you run your own serving stack. You get lower per-hour rates in exchange for owning the ops: deployment, autoscaling, and model tuning are on you. On-demand and reserved rates as of July 2026:

Together GPU Cluster Pricing (per GPU/hr)

| GPU | On-Demand | Reserved (181+ days) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA HGX H100 | $3.99 | $3.09 |
| NVIDIA HGX H200 | $5.99 | $3.99 |
| NVIDIA HGX B200 | $8.19 | $6.79 |

The reserved rate is the real number for a production deployment: a B200 drops from $8.19 to $6.79 per GPU-hour on a 181-day commitment. Clusters make sense when you have the engineering to run the serving stack yourself and the volume to keep the GPUs busy. If you do not want to run the stack, the dedicated endpoint tier adds Together's managed serving on top of these rates.

results.title: Together AI cuts interruptible GPU cluster compute to half price with a five-minute exit window | Beyond the News
highlights:
Together AI now offers preemptible GPU nodes at a fixed 50% discount to on-demand compute, with sub-hour billing, automatic refill and a maximum five-minute drain before reclaim. Current documentation covers Kubernetes and Slurm, but capacity and node lifetime are not guaranteed.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 9 Oct 2026, 6:22 am NZDT 5 min read Copy link

 First published 9 Oct 2026, 6:22 am NZDT 

## Key details

1. September 10, 2026 announcement introduced preemptible compute in Together GPU Clusters.
2. Fixed 50% discount relative to the equivalent on-demand GPU rate, not variable spot bidding.
3. Billing is sub-hourly, metered approximately every one to two minutes.
4. Reclamation drain window is at most five minutes, with SIGTERM on Kubernetes.
5. Current documentation covers Kubernetes and Slurm public previews.
6. Requested preemptible GPU capacity is a target, not a guarantee of allocation.
7. At least one standard node is required; node classes cannot be converted in place.
8. Together attempts automatic refill after reclamation as spare capacity returns.
9. No minimum preemptible-node lifetime is guaranteed during preview.

...

Together AI introduced preemptible GPU nodes for its GPU Clusters in a September 10, 2026 public-preview announcement. The nodes use spare accelerator capacity and are billed at a fixed 50% of the equivalent on-demand rate rather than a fluctuating spot-market price. They can be added to an existing cluster alongside standard nodes, metered in one- to two-minute increments and replenished automatically toward a requested capacity target after reclamation. A reclaim notice starts a drain window of at most five minutes; workloads must checkpoint or finish before removal. The launch announcement focused on Kubernetes, while the current first-party documentation also describes public-preview support for Slurm with job requeue. The lower unit price trades away availability guarantees and predictable uninterrupted execution.

...

- Together does not guarantee a minimum node lifetime or availability of spare GPU capacity.
- The 50% figure is a vendor-published rate discount, not independently measured end-to-end savings.
- Documentation now lists Slurm preview support, but the date that support began is not established by the September announcement.
- Actual checkpoint/retry overhead varies by workload and storage performance.

## What promotions is Together AI running, and when do they end?

Together AI’s pricing page shows one promotion with an end date. Dedicated inference on an NVIDIA HGX H100 costs $3.99 per GPU-hour instead of $5.49, and the page says it’s valid until 09/30/26: 30 September 2026. 1

results.title: Together AI launches preemptible GPU compute at 50 percent off on demand pricing | Awais Khawar
results.author: Awais Khawar
highlights:
# Together AI launches preemptible GPU compute at 50 percent off on demand pricing | Awais Khawar · LinkedIn · 2026-10-11T00:00:00+00:00

**Awais Khawar**: Helping enterprises build agentic AI systems (AWS 3x | Azure 3x | Google AgentSpace & ADK | CrewAI | LangGraph | 5G | WiFi).

---

Together AI launches preemptible GPU compute at 50 percent off on demand pricing

Together AI added a third compute type alongside standard on demand and reserved: preemptible compute, discounted 50 percent off on demand, running on the same underlying NVIDIA GPUs, CPU architecture, and InfiniBand fabric.

The tradeoff is interruption: instances can be taken away with at most five minutes notice. That makes it a fit for burst, short lived work that restarts gracefully: non critical dev and test, batch inference, fine tuning runs lasting minutes to a couple of hours, and research experiments like hyperparameter sweeps.

Operationally it is straightforward. Preemptible capacity is fulfilled asynchronously from spare capacity, so you declare it in the cluster shape and stop polling for availability. Nodes are labeled so you can use affinity rules to keep critical inference pods off preemptible nodes. Billing follows actual usage, so a node alive for a few minutes costs only a few minutes. One constraint: Kubernetes clusters only today, with Slurm support coming.

results.title: Nebius hikes AI cloud prices again as demand for computing power soars | My 95.7
results.author: Thomson Reuters
highlights:
By Thomson Reuters Sep 17, 2026 | 11:16 AM 

Sept 17 (Reuters) – Cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected ​Nvidia chips from October 1, ‌marking the company’s second price hike in three months.

Demand for computing capacity to train and run AI models is surging; rival CoreWeave ‌said ​earlier in the ⁠day that it is ⁠signing contracts at higher prices.

Here are some details:

• Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between ​17% and 21%.

• On-demand rates for some central processing units, made ⁠by AMD and Intel, ⁠and memory offerings have also ​been hiked.

• Prices of some CPU-only instances ​will rise by 25% and those ‌of memory offerings by about 41%, the company said.

• The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm said that customers reserving large-scale clusters ⁠for multiple months can receive commitment discounts.
